land.text: the western colonies: Sardinia, western Sicily, Malta and the Spanish coast

successors.note: 'in the seventh century BC the western colonies came under the control of Carthage' (Phoenicia page); -616 is Cliopatria's last year. The specific pages are later (Sardinia c. 510, southern Iberia after 573); see notes.

land.text: Kition (Larnaca) on Cyprus, a Phoenician city-kingdom until Ptolemy I 'conquered Cyprus in 312 BC and killed Poumyathon, the Phoenician king of Kition'

successors.note: No dossier exists for Kition (or the other Cypriot kingdoms); the cells Cliopatria gives Cyprus in -650..-616 are Kition.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -900..-701: Cliopatria starts in -700. 'From the late tenth century BC, the Phoenicians established commercial outposts throughout the Mediterranean'; Tyre founded colonies in Cyprus, Sardinia, Iberia, the Balearic Islands, Sicily, Malta, Morocco and Tunisia. Two cores have a page: Kition (early Phoenician presence 'at the beginning of the 10th century BC', Kition page) and Gadir (traditionally c. 1100 BC, but 'no archaeological strata on the site can be dated earlier than the 9th century BC', Cadiz page). The Colonies in antiquity page adds Huelva, where Aubet argues for 'a regular presence of Phoenician people from the start of the ninth century BC'. Carthage (814 BC) is a separate state.

correction.text: Kition on Cyprus and Gadir (Cadiz) in Spain, the two oldest Phoenician colonies with a page

keyframe_review.note: 6,352 km2 (Cadiz and Malaga coasts, Motya-Panormus in Sicily, Malta, Tharros in Sardinia) with no Cyprus. Kition was Phoenician from the 10th century ('After c. 850 BC, the city's sanctuaries were rebuilt and reused by Phoenician settlers'), so Cyprus belongs from the start; Cliopatria adds it in -650. History of Sardinia: 'From the 8th century BC' the Phoenicians founded Tharros, Bithia, Sulci, Nora and Caralis, which fits the Tharros cells. The Colonies in antiquity page has no area.

correction.text: the -700 shape plus Kition on Cyprus

keyframe_review.note: 11,441 km2: Sardinia grows from 4 to 16 cells (the Italian count, which includes Sardinia, from 7 to 19). History of Sardinia: the Phoenicians founded cities 'on strategic points in the south and west of Sardinia' from the 8th century BC (Tharros, Bithia, Sulci, Nora, Caralis) without dating each, so the growth is Cliopatria's. Kition is added as in -700.

correction.text: the -675 shape plus Kition on Cyprus

keyframe_review.note: 14,878 km2: Cyprus (3 cells at Kition) joins the shape. The Kition page: Phoenician presence 'under Tyrian rule' from the 10th century; Egyptian domination only from 570. The shape stands to -631.

Unchanged shape to -616. The Phoenicia page: 'in the seventh century BC the western colonies came under the control of Carthage', 'exercised directly through appointed magistrates', so the western part ends within the row's last years; Kition on Cyprus does not pass to Carthage (Kition page: Egyptian rule 570-545, Persian from 545, Ptolemy I in 312).

ledger.note: Late 10th century BC: Tyre begins to plant colonies. 'From the late tenth century BC, the Phoenicians established commercial outposts throughout the Mediterranean.' Cores drawn: Kition on Cyprus (Tyrian presence from the 10th century, Kition page) and Gadir (Cadiz page: traditionally c. 1100 BC, earliest strata 9th century). The year -900 is the end of 'the late tenth century'.

8th-7th century BC: the colonies of the western Mediterranean. Tyre 'founded colonies in Cyprus, Sardinia, Iberia, the Balearic Islands, Sicily, Malta, Morocco, and Tunisia'; History of Sardinia dates the Sardinian cities 'From the 8th century BC'; a wreck of 700 BC lies off Gozo. No page dates the founding of the Sicilian, Maltese, Sardinian or Andalusian settlements one by one; -700 is Cliopatria's first shape.

region.text: the Phoenician coastal settlements of southern Spain, western Sicily, Malta and Sardinia

ledger.note: 7th century BC: more Phoenician towns in Sardinia and Sicily. 'From the 8th century BC' the Phoenicians founded cities 'on strategic points in the south and west of Sardinia' (Tharros, Bithia, Sulci, Nora, Caralis); the page gives no year for any. Cliopatria adds 12 Sardinian cells in -675.

region.text: further Phoenician towns on the south and west coasts of Sardinia and Sicily

ledger.note: The Cypriot colony stays Phoenician. Kition remained a Phoenician city-kingdom under Egyptian (570-545), Persian (545-332) and finally Ptolemaic rule, when 'Ptolemy I conquered Cyprus in 312 BC and killed Poumyathon, the Phoenician king of Kition'. The page does not link Kition to Carthage.

7th century BC: the western Phoenician colonies pass to Carthage. 'in the seventh century BC the western colonies came under the control of Carthage', 'exercised directly through appointed magistrates'. The page gives the century only; -616 is Cliopatria's last year. History of Sardinia puts Carthage's control of Sardinia around 510 BC; the Cadiz page puts the end of Phoenician control of southern Iberia at Tyre's fall in 573.

certainty.note: Trading stations and their hinterlands; no page gives a frontier, an area or a boundary for any colony, so the radius and the Cliopatria cells are drawn soft.

notes:
CLIOPATRIA ROW: one row, -700..-616, 4 shapes, a member of the umbrella (Phoenician Empire). It is an umbrella of unrelated trading towns, not one government: the dossier keeps it as a type colony with no capital. New keyframe -900..-701 (Kition and Gadir) because the pages put the first colonies in the 10th-9th centuries; Kition (Cyprus) is added to the -700 and -675 shapes because Cliopatria adds Cyprus only in -650.
END DATE: the Phoenicia page ('seventh century BC') fits -616 but is the only page for it and is general. The specific pages are later: the Magonid page (Carthage's Sardinian expedition in the mid-520s, the 509 treaty), History of Sardinia (control c. 510), the Cadiz page (Tyre's fall in 573, 'Carthage filled the vacuum'), the Ancient Carthage infobox (independence from Tyre in the mid-6th century). The Carthage dossier bridges with a confidence-1 gain at -616 so that the land does not turn grey; a gap-filler may prefer to extend this row to the 6th century or to split it by colony.
KITION: needs a dossier of its own (Cypriot city-kingdoms, from the 10th century to 312 BC); named as a successor with slug kition. Not written here.
WHAT THE PAGES DO NOT GIVE: dates for the founding of Malta, Motya, Panormus, Solus, Sardinian, Balearic or Moroccan colonies (Mogador and Tingis are named without dates), the Colonies in antiquity page has no Phoenician section beyond Carthage and Huelva, and no page gives an area. Verdicts for -650 and -630 rest on the Kition and Phoenicia pages and stay close to Cliopatria.
WARS: none dated inside -900..-616 on the pages opened (the Sicilian Wars page has a Phoenician-Elymian victory over Selinus and Rhodes in 580 BC, after this row ends, and that page does not tie it to Carthage). The Neo-Assyrian tribute of the Phoenician cities (858-721 BC) and Nebuchadnezzar's siege of Tyre (585-573) concern the homeland, which the phoenicia dossier (me-04) should carry.
PAGE BUDGET: Phoenicia, Colonies in antiquity, Kition, History of Sardinia, Cadiz (five); the Sicilian Wars page was opened for Carthage.
GAZETTEER: Larnaca (Cyprus) and Cadiz resolve as places. Ancient names that the gazetteer lacks: Kition, Gadir, Motya, Panormus, Tharros (Sardinia), Nora, Sulci.
